planting.note: Set divisions or young pot-grown plants in fall into deep, humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist; this species resents disturbance and needs several seasons to build the rootstock before flowering.

directions: Native to woodland margins of eastern and southeastern China, this striking false hellebore sends up pleated, strap-shaped leaves followed by tall, loosely branched flower spikes clad in small deep red to maroon, star-shaped blooms through summer, a notably warmer color than the blackish-purple tones of its better-known relative Veratrum nigrum. The stems and branches carry a distinctive grey-white woolly coating that contrasts with the dark flowers. Grow in a cool, lightly shaded woodland setting with rich, consistently moist soil, and be patient, as clumps take years to bulk up before blooming reliably. Every part of the plant is toxic if ingested, so site it away from grazing animals and curious pets.
